conviction_note: Modest long lean: Funko beat the high end of its own guide in Q1 and Q2 2026 and its Q3 guide (flat sales, adj. EBITDA $25-30M on 43-44% gross margin) looks conservative against last year's $24.4M on a 40.2% margin. The two big toy peers that reported since Funko last spoke (JAKKS +20% sales, Hasbro Consumer Products +4% on Marvel/Spider-Man and KPop Demon Hunters) back that up, and short interest had built to about 7.6M shares (7.6 days to cover) by 30 Sep. Against that: the tariff refunds are already monetised, a new 12.5% Section 301 duty applies, and the refinancing is unresolved. The findings sum to +2.6. The scaled number is (2*0.57-1)*12 = +1.68. p_up is held at 57, a proxy-level lean, because the Q3 beat sits mostly inside the company's own guide and there is no option chain or skew to read.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $250.7M (MarketBeat consensus) / $252.0M (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FNKO/22287, 2026-10-28). That is two roughly agreeing sources, both at the company guide of 'approximately flat' on Q3 2025's $250.9M. EPS consensus is $0.09-0.10. The company's Q3 guide is adj. EBITDA $25-30M and gross margin 43-44%; FY26 guide is net sales flat to +3% and adj. EBITDA $100-110M including the $25.4M Q2 tariff benefit (https://investor.funko.com/news-and-events/press-releases/Press-Releases/2026/Funko-Reports-Strong-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-Reiterates-Full-Year-Net-Sales-Outlook-and-Raises-Adjusted-EBITDA-Guidance/default.aspx, 2026-08-06).
positioning_check: Short interest is snippet_only from CurvedTrading/FINRA (the page returned 403 on fetch): 7.6M shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement with 7.6 days to cover, the highest in its table. It was 6.7M (5.2 days) on 09-15 and 5.2M (5.5 days) on 08-31; Equibles shows 4.26M (6.36 days) on 2026-05-29. Against 56.0M Class A shares outstanding that is about 14%, and a higher share of the true float because TCG holds a large stake. October settlements were not found. On the long side, the activist Pleasant Lake / Fund 1 Investments holds 9.9% in shares plus total-return swaps on 7.29M notional shares (13.0%), about 23% economic exposure (13D/A, 2026-10-16). No usable option chain: skew is null, put/call open-interest ratio 0.77, total open interest 1,159. The stock is -8.67% over 5 days and -6.0% over 20 days into the print, 13.9% below its 52-week high and 117% above its low.

findings.finding: Funko has beaten the top of its own guidance on recent prints: Q2 2026 net sales of $207.7M (+7.4%) beat the high end of its range, and ex-tariff gross margin of 44.4% beat the 42-44% guide. The Q3 guide (sales roughly flat at about $250.9M, gross margin 43-44%, adj. EBITDA $25-30M) looks conservative. Gross margin of 43.5% on flat sales implies about $109M of gross profit against $100.8M in Q3 2025, when adj. EBITDA was $24.4M, and SG&A was falling as a share of sales (38.4% vs 42.5% in Q2). That points to adj. EBITDA at or above the $30M top end, against consensus EPS of $0.09-0.10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints that beat the company's own margin and EBITDA guide rose: 2025-11-06 +10.26% (sales missed, EBITDA held), 2026-05-07 +17.94%, 2026-08-06 +11.36%. The print with a soft guide, 2026-03-12, fell 3.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $250.7-252M sits exactly on the company's 'flat' guide, so the Street has not modelled a beat. Earnings Whispers calls sentiment 'modestly bearish' on margin durability, and the stock is -8.7% over five days into the print. If a beat were priced, consensus would sit above the guide and the stock would be running up, not sliding with short interest building.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 comparison comes from a different document, Funko's Q3 2025 release (https://investor.funko.com/news-and-events/press-releases/Press-Releases/2025/Funko-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results, 2025-11-06): adj. EBITDA $24.4M, gross margin 40.2%. Most of the guide arithmetic rests on the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Two toy peers that reported after Funko last spoke both had strong Q3s. JAKKS Pacific Q3 2026 net sales rose 20% to $254.2M with North America growing (2026-10-22). Hasbro Consumer Products rose 4% to $828M, its fourth straight quarter of growth, led by Marvel, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and KPop Demon Hunters (2026-10-20). Those licences map onto Funko's Q3: it said in August it had incremental Walmart placement tied to Spider-Man, and KPop Demon Hunters blind boxes shipped in September. GameStop's collectibles sales also rose 57% to $356.3M in the quarter to 2026-08-01, although that is mostly trading cards.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of Funko reacting to peer read-throughs. Funko reported its own wholesale point-of-sale units +6% in Q2 and +9% year to date.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved off the flat guide since the peers reported ($252.0M in the 10-28 preview), and FNKO fell from about $6.8 in mid-October to $6.11 after the peer prints. That is the opposite of a priced read-through.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not Funko's own number. The Hasbro source is a different company and document: https://finviz.com/news/404358/hasbro-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results (2026-10-20). GameStop: https://pulse2.com/gamestop-q2-operating-income-hits-record-160-2-million-as-collectibles-sales-jump-57/ (2026-09-08). Hasbro also guided Q4 Consumer Products only flat to slightly up on a tough comparison, which tempers the read-through for Q4.

findings.finding: Unlike Hasbro, which booked about $55M of tariff refunds in Q3, Funko has no further IEEPA refund upside in the quarter. The Q2 10-Q says Funko sold 'substantially all' of its tariff refund receivables ($22.1M of claims for $19.2M). The subsequent $6.3M remitted by CBP 'did not result in additional revenue, gains, or operating cash flows', and the company's total IEEPA tariffs paid are only about $20M. Anyone modelling a Q3 one-off like Hasbro's will find none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print carried the $25.4M tariff benefit and the stock rose 11.36%. That benefit is already in the raised FY EBITDA guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep itself flagged 'check whether Q3 carries more IEEPA refund recognition', and Hasbro's $55M Q3 refund headline invites the comparison. The 10-Q footnote, not the wire copy, is what closes it. If the market expected nothing, no Q3 one-off would appear in previews. None does, so this is mostly priced and is sized small.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the refinancing finding. Hasbro's refund: https://finviz.com/news/404358/hasbro-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results.

findings.finding: New Section 301 forced-labor tariffs of 12.5% on toys from China, Vietnam and Hong Kong took effect on 2026-07-24, replacing the 10% Section 122 surcharge. Funko said on 2026-08-06 that its guidance assumes 10-12% tariffs. The real rate sits at or slightly above the top of that assumption for all of Q3 after July 24 and for Q4, a small gross-margin headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff shocks drove the 2025 sell-offs: -16.43% on 2025-05-08 and -32.79% on 2025-08-07. This change is far smaller and was known when the guide was set.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the rate was in force before the 08-06 guide, and management's '10-12%' presumably reflects it. The residual is the 0.5-point gap and any freight and oil pressure management flagged. Sized near zero.
findings.independence: Management's 10-12% assumption is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15398317687907328, 2026-08-06).

findings.finding: Refinancing is unresolved. The credit agreement matures 2027-12-31; the revolver is fully drawn ($124.6M, 'no remaining borrowing availability'); and the 2.50x max net leverage covenant is tested from the 2026-12-31 quarter, after waivers. The 10-Q says the debt reclassifies to current if it is not amended or refinanced by 2026-12-31. The Q3 release and call are the last scheduled update before that date. Rough covenant arithmetic: net debt of about $160M ($201.1M less $40.7M cash) against trailing adj. EBITDA of roughly $100M including the tariff benefit gives about 1.6x, so there is no visible covenant pressure. That makes the sign roughly neutral: an announced refinancing is upside, silence is a mild overhang.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-02-13 amend-and-extend has no dated reaction in the baseline. The 2026-03-12 print that followed fell 3.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews mention only 'further debt reduction'. None mentions the 12-31 reclassification trigger, which sits in a 10-Q liquidity paragraph. What the money buys is time, not a ramp: it is a maturity extension with no covenant stress visible.
findings.independence: No refinancing news since the February amendment (https://investor.funko.com/news-and-events/press-releases/Press-Releases/2026/Funko-Announces-Amendment-and-Extension-of-Existing-Credit-Agreement/default.aspx, 2026-02-13). Same 10-Q as the tariff-refund finding.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 79% from 4.26M shares (2026-05-29) to 7.6M (2026-09-30, 7.6 days to cover), about 14% of Class A shares outstanding and more of the effective float. Its three previous prints that beat on margins drew +10% to +18% moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +10.26%, +17.94% and +11.36% on the last three margin and EBITDA beats.
findings.why_not_priced: A crowded short is not a fact the market misses, but a squeeze is a reaction mechanism of its own. If the shorts were already covering, short interest would be falling into the print; it was at a table high at the last settlement seen.
findings.independence: Equibles series for the May level: https://equibles.com/stocks/fnko/short-interest. The 5-day drawdown into the print has no identified cause and is worth 0 by itself.

findings.finding: The activist Pleasant Lake (Fund 1 Investments) kept building economic exposure through October. It holds 5,527,297 shares (9.9%), capped near 10%, while its cash-settled swaps grew from 5.25M notional (June) to 6.46M (September) to 7.29M (13.0%, 13D/A of 2026-10-16). It bought shares at $5.63-6.47 in early October. Total economic exposure is about 23%, from a holder that has publicly pushed for strategic alternatives, including a sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The stake has been public since 2026-02-19.
findings.why_not_priced: The swap growth sits in 13D/A Item 6 text that aggregators reduce to '9.9%'. It is not a print catalyst, but a large informed holder adding exposure into the quarter is a mild floor under the reaction. Sized small.
findings.independence: The earlier amendments are separate filings: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1704711/000092189526002624/0000921895-26-002624.txt (2026-09-22) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1704711/000092189526001629/0000921895-26-001629.txt (June 2026).

findings.finding: CEO Josh Simon sold 181,893 shares on 2026-09-03 at about $5.76-5.87 (about $1.05M), cutting his direct holding to 151,440 shares. The sale followed an exercise or vesting of 333,333 shares on 2026-09-01, and an aggregator says it covered tax withholding.
findings.why_not_priced: A public Form 4, so mostly priced. A vesting-linked sale carries little information about the quarter.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide implies a soft Q4. Net sales flat to +3% on FY25's $908.2M, less H1 sales of $408.6M and a flat Q3 (about $250.9M), leaves Q4 2026 at $248.6-276.0M, which is -9% to +1% against Q4 2025's $273.1M (itself -7% YoY). Implied Q4 adj. EBITDA is $17.8-32.8M against $23.3M. A beat in Q3 alongside a reiterated FY range would itself be an implied raise, which leaves room to hold or lift the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide changes have decided this stock. The 2026-03-12 initial FY26 guide (flat to +3%) drew -3.95%. The 2026-08-06 EBITDA raise drew +11.36%. The 2025 guide withdrawals and cuts drew -16% to -33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews cite the FY range but not the Q4 residual. If the market read the Q4 bar as soft, consensus FY revenue ($927.8M per Benzinga, at the top half of the range) would already sit above a flat-Q3 path. As it stands, a Q3 beat with a held range is the base case and a raise is upside.
findings.independence: H1 and Q3 inputs come from the Q2 release (a different document). Management said Q4 holiday visibility is lower and Q2/Q3 2025 shipments were distorted by catch-up orders, which tempers the easy-comp read; Hasbro guided Q4 Consumer Products flat to slightly up.

outside_window.finding: Proposal from the US-China Board of Trade (announced 2026-09-25) to include toys, HTSUS 9503.0000, in tariff relief on $30B of non-sensitive Chinese goods. It is a recommendation only, with no rates and no effective date; a Federal Register notice is required first.
outside_window.resolves_by: unknown (after a Federal Register notice; not dated inside the window)

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The long lean runs against the -8.7% five-day and -6% twenty-day drift into the print, but agrees with the name's recent reaction function (three margin beats bought for +10% to +18%) and with the crowded short.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): Q3 beat finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2. Not further, because this name has paid for margin beats (rule 1 reaction history is supportive).
Rule 5 (proxy): peer read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.5. Tariff-rate proxy cut from -0.4 to -0.2 because it was also known at guide time.
Rule 2 (one-off): tariff-refund absence cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): refinancing re-signed from -0.3 to 0.0 after the leverage check (about 1.6x vs the 2.5x covenant, no going-concern flag).
Rule 5 (unexplained drawdown is worth 0) and rule 7 (squeeze is a mechanism): positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, carrying the short-interest part only.
Activist finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, and implied-Q4 guide finding from +0.6 to +0.5 (arithmetic inference, not a document number).
Rule 8: abs_move_pct kept at 12, not lowered; p_up moved from 58 to 57.
